passages.context: Aquinas's endorsement of the anti-theft argument on Chrysostom's authority, read in the retrieved page within section 87552, with the preceding allegory of the sudarium and the following exposition of the other disciple's entry in view.
passages.notes: The reference ut habetur Matth. ult., 13, which stands in the delivered text at the end of the first sentence, is omitted from the transcription. The clause praecipue cum oportuisset eos festinanter hoc facere propter praesentiam custodum is not in the Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers text of Chrysostom's homily; the corresponding detail about the guards stands in Theophylact's comment on Luke 24:12.

alternate_titles: Commentary on the Gospel of John
work.author: Thomas Aquinas
work.description: Aquinas's commentary on the Fourth Gospel, a reportatio of his lectures. Chapter 20, lecture 1 treats John 20:1-10: it endorses the argument that the disposition of the cloths excludes theft, expressly on Chrysostom's authority and with the added detail of the guards' presence, and it then reports both Augustine's and Chrysostom's readings of he saw and believed, giving Augustine's as the resolution and Chrysostom's as an alternative. A locus is chapter.lecture.
work.title: Super Evangelium S. Ioannis lectura
